description: The Groundwater Monitoring Tool, GWMT, is an open-source Android tool on the India Observatory site that lets users collect water level data of wells and pool it on a web platform for public access. The page sets out the problem: India uses about a quarter of the world's groundwater, groundwater supplies 70 percent of agriculture and 85 percent of drinking water, yet groundwater level data for most of the country are unavailable, and location-specific data are needed to move from groundwater development to management. The tool uses a standard methodology for data collection to keep data quality consistent and pools data from decentralised sources; the page offers the app for download, a public app and a campaign. Coverage: India, wherever users contribute. Access: free app and web platform; open source is stated but the licence is not named on the page read. Caveats: data quality depends on contributors, and the number of wells or data access terms were not stated on the page read. It supports groundwater level calibration for aquifer and irrigation simulations, and lists no linked catalogue records.
